claims.text: SPS consolidation of ZrB2–AlFeNiCoCr at approximately 1700°C will produce a refined multiphase microstructure.
The proposed processing route will improve densification at approximately 1700°C.
The proposed cermet will have enhanced structural integrity.
The proposed cermet will develop protective surface oxides.
The proposed cermet will have greater oxidation resistance than single-phase ZrB2 and prior lower-temperature specimens.
The proposed cermet will have greater durability against liquid plating-metal corrosion than single-phase ZrB2 and prior lower-temperature specimens.
The AlFeNiCoCr binder will form a continuous network within a finely dispersed multiphase microstructure.
The continuous AlFeNiCoCr binder network will promote grain-boundary strengthening.
Sintering at approximately 1700°C will restrict grain growth.
Sintering at approximately 1700°C will restrict phase decomposition.
The AlFeNiCoCr binder will aid densification of the ZrB2-based body.
Under service exposure, the binder will oxidize to form a thin, adherent protective layer.
The refined microstructure and protective layer will limit pathways for oxidation.
The refined microstructure and protective layer will limit pathways for liquid-metal corrosion.
The cermet sintered at approximately 1700°C will have strength comparable to or greater than the stated reference materials.
Single-phase ZrB2 typically requires sintering above 2300°C to achieve densification.
Single-phase ZrB2 lacks sufficient oxidation resistance for the target application.
Single-phase ZrB2 lacks sufficient liquid-metal corrosion resistance for the target application.
Unmodified ZrB2 specimens prepared near 1700°C have compromised structural integrity and durability.
The proposed cermet is expected to perform reliably during oxidation exposure up to approximately 1200°C.
